name: Critical Minerals Facility

evidence.note: "the expanded $5 billion Critical Minerals Facility, which provides government-backed loans and equity support for projects"

notes: The release does not name the body that administers the Facility, so none is recorded.

name: Critical Minerals Production Tax Incentive
legalAuthorityAsStated: Future Made in Australia (Production Tax Credits and Other Measures) Act 2025, Schedule 2, inserting Division 419 into the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997

evidence.note: "Schedule 2—Critical minerals production tax incentive"; a refundable tax offset for registered processing activities.

name: Critical Minerals Strategic Reserve

evidence.locator: First and seventh to ninth paragraphs
evidence.note: "The Reserve will operate by securing rights to minerals produced in Australia and on-selling those rights"; "Future transactions under the Reserve will be led out of the Department of Industry, Science and Resources, in close partnership with Export Finance Australia."

notes: Export Finance Australia's partnership role is kept in this note; it has no registry record until a cited source states what kind of body it is.

name: Critical Minerals Research, Development and Demonstration (CMRDD) program

evidence.note: "Funding for these projects comes from NRCan’s Critical Minerals Research, Development and Demonstration Program (CMRDD). The CMRDD is part of the Canadian Critical Minerals Strategy"
One stream funds federal laboratories' research and development, the other is contribution funding to outside projects. The page does not say here whether contributions are repayable.
"from geoscience and exploration to mineral processing, manufacturing and recycling applications, including support for research, development and technological deployment"
"Budget 2022 provided $3.8 billion over eight years to implement the Canadian Critical Minerals Strategy."

name: Office of Strategic Capital critical-minerals lending (One Big Beautiful Bill Act)

evidence.note: "The bill provides OSC with $500 million of credit subsidy funding, creating up to $100 billion in available loan funds specifically for critical minerals production and related industries and projects."
A descriptive name: the sources give this lending no programme title.
